description: Table 1 is a single-panel image of a tabular data block, not a plot: a header row of six element symbols (C, Mn, Al, S, P, Fe) separated by one horizontal rule from a single data row. The data row reads, left to right, 0.97, 27.91, 8.04, 0.004, 0.006, and "Bal.". The caption supplies the unit as wt% and identifies the table as the chemical composition of the test steel, so the row reads C 0.97, Mn 27.91, Al 8.04, S 0.004, P 0.006 wt%, Fe balance. All cells are fully legible at the supplied resolution; no axes, legend, scale bar, uncertainty or measurement method is printed, and there are no sub-panels. The table's role is to define the alloy studied: the citing text names it the low-density experimental Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C (in wt%) steel, referred to as "test steel", produced by melting and casting in a vacuum furnace, then heated to 1200 °C for 2 h and hot forged into 100 × 100 mm billets, with a determined density of 6.82 g cm⁻³. The table therefore supplies the nominal composition underpinning all cryogenic-rolling results in the paper.

subfigures.description: A two-row table: header cells C, Mn, Al, S, P, Fe above a single data row reading 0.97, 27.91, 8.04, 0.004, 0.006, Bal., with a horizontal rule between them. Unit given only in the caption as wt%.

observations.observation: The header row of Table 1 lists six element symbols in the order C, Mn, Al, S, P, Fe.
The single data row gives 0.97 under C, 27.91 under Mn, 8.04 under Al, 0.004 under S, 0.006 under P, and 'Bal.' under Fe.
A single horizontal rule separates the header row from the data row; the image contains no other text, axes, scale bar or legend.
The caption states the values are in wt% and that the table is the chemical composition of the test steel.
Iron is reported only as 'Bal.' (balance), so no numeric Fe content is printed.
The citing text names the alloy as the low-density experimental Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C (in wt%) steel, referred to as 'test steel', produced by melting the ingredients and casting in a vacuum furnace.
The citing text states the ingot was first heated to 1200 °C and held for 2 h, then hot forged into billets of 100 × 100 mm cross-section.
The citing text states the density of the test steel was determined to be 6.82 g cm⁻³; this value appears nowhere in the table image.
Mn (27.91) and Al (8.04) are the two largest alloying additions, while S (0.004) and P (0.006) are at impurity level.

measured_quantities: chemical composition (wt%) of C, Mn, Al, S, P
